The critic re-implemented the plan's §4.9 sketch independently and replayed it
over the full parse-fail-mentioning plan corpus (291 persisted plans). Both
Must-Fix items are defects on REAL persisted plans, not hypotheticals.

## Must-Fix 1 — comma-truncation → arm count 0 → ZeroDivisionError wedges the
## whole no-flags verify_plan run (4 real plans)

`_C70_ARMN_RE` (`\b(\d+)\s+arms?\b`) matches "arms" used as a VERB and
truncates comma-grouped numbers: `tasks/awaiting_promotion/2054/plans/v9.md:198`
reads "a projection < 9,000 arms the contingency wave preemptively", which
captures `000` → the window resolves exactly one distinct arm count, **0** →
`slice // n_arms` raises ZeroDivisionError. #2054 v9-v12 are `kind: experiment`,
so the check is ARMED on them.

`verify_plan_text` (`scripts/verify_plan.py:13853-13858`) runs `chk(raw, kind)`
with no exception containment, so this takes down the ENTIRE run that feeds the
Step 9c gate — the #1388 fleet-wedge shape reached via an exception instead of
a FAIL. Acceptance criterion 2 ("never returns passed=False") is satisfied
VACUOUSLY by a check that raises instead of returning.

Same comma-truncation family produces silent FALSE LOW reads elsewhere:
"1,000 draws/arm" → DIRECT captures `000` → per_arm=0; "10,150 draws" → TOTAL
reads 150.

Fix: (i) new SKIP branch on `n_arms == 0`; (ii) extend EVERY numeric-capture
lookbehind to `(?<![\d.,])` — ARMN, TOTAL, COMPONENT digits, and both DIRECT
alternatives; (iii) guard the verb usage (`arms?\b(?!\s+the\b)` — the corpus
also has "3 arms the driver", a non-zero false count); (iv) fixture embedding
the real v9:198+204 text asserting no-raise AND SKIP.

## Must-Fix 2 — the FIXED #2162 revisions (v8/v9/v10) all false-WARN, and
## acceptance criterion 5 would misclassify them as true positives

v8 RESIZED the pilot 150→540 (v8:48-49, "60/arm × 3 arms … ⇒ 60 effective
draws", ≥ 51 — satisfiable, i.e. the defect was FIXED in v8). But v8:672 /
v10:686 carry the house-mandated decision-rationale quote *"(v7's 150-draw
config gave ~30/arm — one …)"*: `_C70_DIRECT_RE` matches "~30/arm",
short-circuits the arm-count path, and §4.7's "ANY resolved evaluation failing
⇒ WARN" overrides the coexisting 60/arm PASS evaluation. Corpus replay: v8, v9,
v10 all WARN at (30, 51). Neither escape applies — escape 1 ("no judge-pilot
gate") is false, escape 2 is arm-count-only and DIRECT bypasses arm count.

This inverts the check's purpose: house convention REQUIRES quoting the
superseded value in §11 rationale / amendment notes, so every future plan that
fixes this exact defect and documents the fix re-WARNs permanently. The check
would fire loudest on plans that already fixed the defect.

Compounding: plan §6 acceptance criterion 5 says "#2162 v7 (and its later
revisions, if the sizing survived) WARN" — the sizing did NOT survive (fixed in
v8), so the criterion as written primes the implementer to accept three false
WARNs as expected true positives.

Fix: (a) third standalone escape with a historical/superseded tail; (b) pin a
corrected-plan fixture (fixed gate + the verbatim v10:686-shaped quote); (c)
correct criterion 5's expected set — v7 = true WARN, v8-v10 = the false-WARN
class the escape must silence.

## Verified-good (the critic checked these rather than assuming)

Helper line refs, `_standalone_na_declared` signature, c69-as-final-CHECKS-entry,
`chk(raw, kind)` call shape, c70 free, `judge_pilot.py`'s
`max(min_effective, floor(1/t)+1)` refusal + its "Multi-rubric waves call the
gate ONCE PER RUBRIC" docstring, `_refusal_resolution_floor`'s float-trap
docstring, and fixture lines 477/481/483/484/489/490 verbatim. A1/A2 traces
REPRODUCE exactly under independent re-implementation (per_arm=20, required=51,
WARN fires; the tightened DIRECT lookbehind correctly rejects `0.10 per arm`
and `72 pairs/arm`). Exact-Fraction arithmetic correct at 2%→51, 3%→34,
1.5%→67. Min-slice reading confirmed faithful to the helper's own contract.

FN-e's premise verified EMPIRICALLY over the corpus: parse-fail thresholds are
238×2%, 3×1%; the only two >10% hits are #1934 (`kind: infra`, a kill criterion
on a measured rate, not a pilot gate — kind-gated out anyway). So dropping the
`max(min_effective_draws_per_arm=10, ...)` leg is empirically safe.

## Nice-to-have (non-blocking, to be weighed in the revise)

1. The check MISSES the #2054 pilot itself (~200 draws / "the 4 character arms"
   / 2% → 50/arm, genuinely sub-resolution): "4 character arms" has an
   adjective between digit and noun, so `\d+ arms` does not match. Accepted-FN
   class — add to the docstring FN list rather than widening ARMN.
2. The `allow_subresolution_pilot` early-return short-circuits later anchors, so
   a plan with one declared-subresolution gate plus a second genuinely
   defective gate PASSes. Prefer `continue`-with-recorded-PASS over `return`.
3. Cross-item pairing channels beyond arm count (a neighbouring gate's
   component-form draws; a neighbouring "per arm" token upgrading an aggregate
   threshold) have no escape — MF2's escape tail could be worded generically
   enough to cover both.
4. Calibration scan should record the matched source tuple
   (direct/component/total + values) for non-SKIP PASS rows too, so
   satisfaction-via-wrong-window is adjudicable (#937 matched-satisfier
   convention; #2329's two windows resolved different (draws, arms) pairings,
